title: Invertibility of the specified finite comparison
statement: Fix universes $d,t,u$, a prime $\ell$, a field $E$ finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $Y$ in universe $t$, a finite-field datum $D$ of characteristic $p$ in universe $d$, and $\ell\ne p$. On the small pro-etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_Y$ be the coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(B)$ and $D(B_n)$ of module sheaves at coefficient universe $\max(u,t+1)$. Write $H_B,H_{B_n}$ for the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $F_n:D(B)\to D(B_n)$ for derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and $Q$ for complex localization. For every tensor presentation $a$ of $B$, every $n\ge0$, every reduction presentation $m$ from $a$ at level $n$ [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models], and arbitrary $K,L\in D(B)$, the specified transpose $c_{n,K,L}:F_nH_B(K,L)\to H_{B_n}(F_nK,F_nL)$ is invertible. No completeness or boundedness condition is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the chain-representative theorem to the given presentations and K,L. It supplies the supported rank-one coefficient complex, the signed chain map f, and the square identifying the restricted specified comparison with its localization.

proof.text: Apply the degreewise signed Hom-tensor calculation to each component f^j. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components makes f an isomorphism. Localization preserves this isomorphism. The normalization square and cancellation of the endpoint isomorphisms show that the restricted comparison is invertible.

proof.text: Scalar restriction preserves finite limits and colimits. Its composition with the forgetful functor to sheaves is the finite-coefficient forgetful functor, which reflects isomorphisms. Thus scalar restriction reflects isomorphisms on modules. Exactness identifies its application to every cohomology map with cohomology of the restricted derived map. Reflect these cohomology isomorphisms and apply the derived-category cohomology criterion to conclude that the original specified comparison is invertible.
